svg.title: The Git origin of an OCI source is declared
svg.desc: Overview of ADR-0044, proposed. CI builds an artifact from a Git repository and pushes it to a registry; Flux pulls it through an OCIRepository and a Kustomization applies it. The executor reads the Kustomization and the OCIRepository status in the cluster, the declaration in RemediationSettings spec.ociSources (the Git repository and path the artifact is built from), and the Git repository through the Git App. The artifact's source and revision annotations are only compared with the declaration. No declaration ends NeedsIntervention with OCIOriginNotDeclared, a difference of source, ref or commit ends it with OCIOriginMismatch, an artifact Flux did not verify, or verified with a keyless signature and no identity named, ends it with OCISourceUnverified unless the declaration says verification NotRequired, an artifact without annotations ends it with OCIOriginUnrecorded, an OCIRepository the executor may not read ends it with OCISourceNotReadable, each with no Git write. An OCIRepository whose spec.ref sets a digest, semver or semverFilter ends SourceNotBranch, as the Git rule does; only a tag passes. With the opt-in strict mode (objectFrom DeclaredRepository) the OCIRepository must itself be listed in the inventory of a Kustomization of the declared repository with a live spec equal to the file in Git, or the request ends OCISourceNotFromGit. A match continues with the ordinary source mapping and opens a pull request in the declared repository and path. A verified artifact proves only that Flux accepted a signer the writer of the OCIRepository chose. After the merge an OCI unit counts as applied only while its current artifact passes the same verification check (unless NotRequired) and the live value matches the desired one; if it does not by the end of the window the request ends DeliveryNotObserved, and an OCIRepository read that stays refused ends it DeliveryNotChecked. Only the OCIRepository read is behind the opt-in grant. The executor never reads the registry, the artifact content, any secret or the artifact's URL.
svg.text: DELIVERY (NOT CHANGED)
Git repository
CI builds from it
Registry
flux push artifact
OCIRepository
status.artifact: revision, metadata
Kustomization
applies the artifact to the workload
Executor reads three things
1. Kustomization and OCIRepository (get):
Ready, verified, tag ref, applied revision, annotations.
Only the OCIRepository read is opt-in, off by default.
2. RemediationSettings spec.ociSources:
the repository and path the artifact is built from;
strict mode (opt-in): the OCIRepository is in Git too.
3. The Git repository, through the Git App:
branch head, ancestry of the annotated commit,
the declaring file. No new App permission.
The annotations are compared, never obeyed
NO DECLARATION
NeedsIntervention, OCIOriginNotDeclared: the message says what to declare. No Git write.
NOT VERIFIED BY FLUX (UNLESS NotRequired)
NeedsIntervention, OCISourceUnverified: unset, not verified, or no identity named. No Git write.
DECLARATION AND ARTIFACT DISAGREE
NeedsIntervention, OCIOriginMismatch: source, ref (the target branch) or commit. No Git write.
ARTIFACT WITHOUT ANNOTATIONS
NeedsIntervention, OCIOriginUnrecorded: not accepted on the declaration alone. No Git write.
OCIREPOSITORY NOT READABLE
NeedsIntervention, OCISourceNotReadable: the opt-in grant is off. No Git write.
THEY AGREE
The ordinary mapping goes on: a pull request in the declared repository and path.
AFTER THE MERGE (OCI UNIT)
Applied only while the current artifact is verified
and the live value matches the desired one.
Not by the end of the window: DeliveryNotObserved.
A refused read: DeliveryNotChecked.
Never
the registry, with or without credentials; the artifact's content or its URL; any Secret, ServiceAccount or secretRef of the OCIRepository;
a repository, path or branch taken from an annotation; a signature check of its own (Flux verifies; it does not prove the origin). Analyzer and verifier get no new read.
